subject.title: feat(cron): configurable minimum interval guardrail for recurring jobs

question: Should OpenClaw accept `cron.minInterval` as a core default-off config contract for recurring jobs now?
rationale: The implementation is concrete, but root policy treats new config/default surfaces and fail-closed scheduling behavior as compatibility-sensitive product direction.

options.title: Accept Default-Off Guardrail
options.body: After the docs map is refreshed, land `cron.minInterval` as an opt-in core config with create/update rejection and fire-time pacing.

options.title: Keep Warning-Only Direction
options.body: Reject core enforcement for now and pursue advisory warnings or a narrower follow-up under the umbrella issue.

options.title: Defer And Split
options.body: Pause this PR while the cron/session accumulation umbrella is split into retention, warning, and enforcement decisions.

recommendation.title: Accept Default-Off Guardrail
recommendation.body: After the docs map is refreshed, land `cron.minInterval` as an opt-in core config with create/update rejection and fire-time pacing.
